summary.headline: Artemis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12.7% to INR 287.32 crore, PAT up 48.3% to INR 31.44 crore, EBITDA margin 21.5%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 287.32 crore (+12.7% YoY), with Gurugram standalone up 15.4%, and EBITDA of INR 61.82 crore at a 21.5% margin. PAT rose 48.3% YoY to INR 31.44 crore. Gurugram occupancy was 65.7% and ARPOB-linked ARPOB (average revenue per occupied bed) was INR 85,690. Artemis Shanti Hospital in Raipur (300 beds) went live in July 2026, with OPD from 9 July and theatres/cath labs from 27 July. Management also announced a 200+ bed Tower IV in Gurugram and an INR 700 crore enabling resolution for a QIP, which is expected 6-8 months out.

segments.name: Gurugram flagship (tertiary/quaternary)
segments.commentary: Contributes 95-97% of revenue per management. Occupancy 65.7% and ARPOB INR 85,690 in Q1; management expects margin to reach 20-21% in FY27 and 23-24% over 2-3 years.

segments.name: Artemis Shanti Hospital, Raipur (300 beds)
segments.commentary: Newly operational: OPD from 9 July 2026, theatres and cath labs from 27 July. Capex INR 120 crore, about 80% spent; breakeven expected in 15-18 months with operating loss of around INR 20 crore.

segments.name: Smaller centres (Artemis Lite, Cardiac Care, Daffodils)
segments.commentary: Management described performance as muted due to capacity constraints in small units. Segment revenue and margin were not disclosed on the call; the analyst was asked to request them offline from the CFO.

segments.name: International patients
segments.commentary: Close to 27% of revenue in Q1 despite West Asia disruption; management guides to 30% or more in Q2 and adds 2-3 new country fronts a year.

guidance_outlook: Gurugram margin expected at 20-21% in FY27 and 23-24% over the next 2-3 years; management said upwards of 23% at the 900-1,000 bed scale.
Gurugram occupancy targeted at 70% by Q2 FY27, with management saying it is on track.
Tower IV (200+ beds, Gurugram) expected to be operational in 18-22 months; breakeven in 8-10 months and 50% utilisation in the first six months after launch, per management.
Raipur expected to break even in 15-18 months with about INR 20 crore operating loss; direct insurance empanelment expected in 8-10 weeks.

Total capex of about INR 800 crore over three years (FY27-FY29) including Raipur, Tower IV, VIMHANS and parking, with INR 250 crore VIMHANS deposit additional; INR 700 crore QIP enabling resolution expected 6-8 months out.
Target of about 2,000 operational beds by 2029-30 across Gurugram Tower IV, Raipur and planned South Delhi / VIMHANS projects.
capex_capacity: Tower IV Gurugram: 200+ beds plus multi-level parking, capex about INR 55 lakh per bed (INR 50-55 lakh range), total about INR 120 crore for the tower.
Multi-level parking INR 70-80 crore; replacement capex INR 100-120 crore over three years, per management's breakdown of the INR 800 crore plan.

Raipur: 300 beds, total capex INR 120 crore, 80% spent; PET-CT installation and radiotherapy unit (about six months to transport) pending, with services going live between 10 August and end-August 2026.
VIMHANS (650 beds) pure capex INR 350-360 crore plus about INR 250 crore deposit, of which INR 130 crore already paid; remaining IFC-raised money to be deposited to VIMHANS by year-end.
demand_pricing: Gurugram ARPOB is among the highest in Delhi NCR; growth attributed to case-mix shift toward quaternary procedures and fewer average length-of-stay days.
Management cited economies of scale (cost base steady while admitting more patients) and case mix as margin drivers; smaller centres a relatively small contributor.
International business held up despite the West Asia war: 27% share of patients in Q1, with the top line up 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the international patient mix come off, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said international share was close to 27% in Q1 despite West Asia flight disruption; it sees Q2 at 30% or better, with 2-3 new country fronts added each year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 200-bed FAR expansion a function of new height/FAR rules, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Tower IV combines 130-150 free beds from Platinum green-building FAR with about 70 beds of purchased FAR; full operationalisation in 18-22 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can Gurugram margins reach 20-21% in FY27 and 23-24% over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered yes to both; it expects the Gurugram margin to exceed 21% after the 200-bed addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Raipur ramp-up and the expected breakeven and loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven in 15-18 months with about INR 20 crore operating loss; all services launched together, with insurance empanelment expected in 8-10 weeks and an interim cashless intermediary in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the QIP be postponed given only half of the IFC money is spent?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 700 crore is an enabling resolution; the remaining IFC money will be deposited to VIMHANS by year-end, and the QIP is 6-8 months out depending on brownfield asset finalisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is Tower IV capex per bed and the FY27-FY29 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 55 lakh per bed including parking; total FY27-FY29 capex including Raipur is about INR 800 crore, excluding the VIMHANS deposit.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 800 crore capex is attributable to each project?
qa_highlights.answer: Raipur INR 120 crore, VIMHANS INR 350-360 crore, Tower IV about INR 120 crore, parking INR 70-80 crore, replacement capex INR 100-120 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Daffodils and Artemis Lite muted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small units face capacity constraints; some centres (e.g., New Friends Colony) are being consolidated, and the model will be hub-and-spoke for new cities.
